input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 (p0080) is the only assignment provision in the agreement; Section 2's licence grant is non-exclusive and does not separately restrict transfer, and there is no change-of-control, re-pricing or successors-and-assigns language anywhere (the term and termination provisions at p0078-p0079 contain no change-of-control trigger), so TrueLink has no exit right on our change of control and that element needs no change. The clause is mutual and already requires consent for assignments, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the only carve-out is an assignment to a "financially responsible affiliate", so we could not assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets - the absence of an M&A carve-out is walk-away territory under this rule; and (ii) approval is unqualified, giving TrueLink an absolute veto rather than a not-unreasonably-withheld standard. The redline makes the shortest change to reach the fallback: a mutual successor-in-interest carve-out on written notice plus a reasonableness standard on approval of other assignments, leaving the affiliate carve-out and the rest of Section 15 untouched. We have not pursued the preferred asymmetric position (Vendor consent-only, no assignment to a competitor) because the mutual fallback is acceptable and the smaller edit.

proposal.summary: Section 15: add a mutual successor carve-out on written notice and a reasonableness standard on assignment approval.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 lets either party block an assignment for any reason and carves out only affiliates, so we cannot assign to a successor in a merger or sale of our business. We have added a mutual successor carve-out on written notice and made approval of other assignments subject to a not-unreasonably-withheld standard; this is our fallback position and leaves the affiliate carve-out intact.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest, upon written notice to the other party.

mappings.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
A successor assignment requires written notice.
